verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: `isTimeout` only treats `DOMException` named `TimeoutError` as retryable, so a connection reset (ECONNRESET) is not retried and the probe reports the upstream down on the first reset. WHY: Node/undici surfaces a reset keep-alive socket as a generic `TypeError: fetch failed` (with `err.cause`), not a `DOMException`, so `isTimeout` returns false, `probeUpstream` returns false immediately, and `router.ts:8` fails closed with a 503 for every request until the next 30 s refresh — the exact lockout the retry was added to prevent. HOW: also retry when the error (or its `cause`) indicates a transient network failure, e.g. check `err?.cause?.code === 'ECONNRESET'`/`'ECONNREFUSED'`/`'ETIMEDOUT'` alongside the TimeoutError check.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The finding re-raises the exact problem already posted in PreviousReviewDecisions entry round-a-P30-probe-retries-timeouts-only: a single transient network error (timeout or ECONNRESET) marks the auth upstream unhealthy and router.ts fails closed with a 503 for every request until the next 30s refresh. That entry explicitly names ECONNRESET from a recycled keep-alive socket, and its outcome is "partially_implemented" — the developer added a retry loop but only gated it on `isTimeout`. This candidate finding blames the incomplete fix (isTimeout covering only TimeoutError, not ECONNRESET) and describes the identical failure in the identical operation (probe marks upstream down → 503 lockout). Per the repeat rule, that same crash/wrong-result in the same operation is that entry again, so it must be dropped.
